span.label: the approach assumes a task-specific similarity metric, which is hard to define
span.note: what this limits: every guarantee the framework offers: it assumes Quotation withheld - supplied from outside the definition

span.label: Obtaining or justifying the task-specific similarity metric the framework depends on is the hardest part, and any real metric will be an approximation.
span.note: what this limits: the practical applicability of the whole approach: JUSTIFYING THE AVAILABILITY OF OR ACCESS TO THE DISTANCE METRIC ... IS ONE OF THE MOST CHALLENGING ASPECTS OF OUR FRAMEWORK, AND IN REALITY THE METRIC USED WIL[l be imperfect]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The general fairness LP gives no quantitative bound on the loss it incurs.
span.note: what this limits: the loss claim for the general fairness LP: THE RESULT HOWEVER DOES NOT GIVE A CONCRETE QUANTITATIVE BOUND ON THE RESULTING LOSS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: When the protected set is far from the rest of the population under the metric, satisfying the Lipschitz condition can still leave unfair practices unchecked.
span.note: what this limits: the protection guarantee for a distant protected set: IF MEMBERS OF S ARE RELATIVELY FAR FROM THE MEMBERS OF T ACCORDING TO THE DISTANCE METRIC, THEN SATISFYING THE LIPSCHITZ CONDITION MAY FAIL TO PREVENT SOME OF THE UNFAIR[ness]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: No tight Earthmover characterisation is obtained for the relative-infinity distance version of the bias.
span.note: what this limits: the Earthmover characterisation: for biasD-infinity WE DO NOT GET A TIGHT CHARACTERIZATION
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The whole treatment assumes one metric applied uniformly to everyone; per-user or plural metrics are untested.
span.note: what this limits: the scope of every result in the paper: OUR DISCUSSION THROUGHOUT THIS PAPER HAS ASSUMED THAT A SINGLE METRIC IS USED ACROSS THE BOARD - per-user or plural metrics are untested
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The nearest existing similarity system the authors point to (AALIM, health care) does not supply the kind of distance metric the framework needs.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that a metric could be obtained in practice: the nearest existing system DOES NOT (YET?) PROVIDE THE DISTANCE METRIC THAT OUR APPROACH REQUIRES
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A widely used fairness criterion can hold while the outcome is, in the authors' words, blatantly unfair to an individual.
span.note: what this limits: statistical parity used as evidence that a classifier is fair: the authors give examples in which statistical parity is maintained while the outcome from an individual's point of view is blatantly unfair
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The metric the formal guarantee consumes is a social agreement that is expected to change.
span.note: what this limits: any fairness guarantee obtained in this framework: when ground truth is unavailable the metric may reflect the best available approximation as agreed upon by society, and is assumed to be public and open to continual refinement
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The bridge from individual fairness to group fairness holds only under a stated distance condition.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that individual fairness delivers group fairness: it holds Quotation withheld
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The population the metric is defined over is a modelling choice the authors flag.
span.note: what this limits: the scope of the fairness guarantee proved here: the authors state they have assumed the set is that of real individuals rather than all possible encodings of individuals

span.label: fairness - INDIVIDUAL VERSUS GROUP, AND THE SECOND CAN HOLD WHILE THE FIRST FAILS: individual fairness is the principle that two people similar for a task be classified similarly, statistical parity is a property of demographics in aggregate, and the paper's examples keep the second while the first is blatantly violated

span.label: the similarity metric - AS SOCIETY'S CURRENT BEST APPROXIMATION: where no ground truth exists the metric stands in for one by agreement, is meant to be public and revisable, and is the input on which every formal result in the paper depends

span.label: fairness as a principle - TREAT SIMILAR INDIVIDUALS SIMILARLY: the paper's whole notion is one sentence, and everything formal in it is machinery for making 'similar' precise, which is why the metric carries the weight rather than the definition
